neighbours.label: a noun naming a part or format of a notation while explaining how to read it ('the bottom number', 'the first three digits', 'single quotes'); the same topics without naming a notation part stay low
fire: On a fraction, the top number tells you how many parts you have.
In a tire size like 205/55, the first number is the width in millimetres.
On a time signature, the lower number shows which note gets one beat.
In a postcode, the last two digits identify the local delivery office.
When you read a vitamin label, the second number gives the daily percentage.
In an IP address, the first three digits often point to the network.
On a dress pattern, the middle number is the waist measurement.
In a chess move like Nf3, the capital letter names the piece that moves.
quiet: Cut the cake into eight parts so everyone gets the same amount.
The tires on this car are wide and quiet on the highway.
The band played slowly so the dancers could keep the beat.
The local delivery office closes at five on weekdays.
This vitamin is taken once a day with a meal.
The network went down twice during the storm last night.
She measured her waist before ordering the dress online.
He moved the knight early and won the game quickly.
